summary: The note previews the Local Business Fair on September 10th, 2023, at the newly renovated Jackson Park, showcasing more than 150 local businesses. Beyond selling, the fair offers panels, workshops, funding consultations, a Youth Entrepreneur Zone and a Green Marketplace, with an emphasis on inclusion, sustainability and community networking. It frames the event as a response to pressure from big-box stores and franchises and as a reflection of the town's resilient economy.
one_line: The September 10th, 2023 Local Business Fair at Jackson Park showcases 150+ local businesses with education, funding access, inclusivity and sustainability themes.
key_facts: The Local Business Fair is scheduled for September 10th, 2023.
The fair is organized by Sarah Jennings, Marko Chen, and Leslie Rivera, who are on the town's small business development council.
The fair will be held at the newly renovated Jackson Park and will feature more than 150 local businesses.
Exhibitors include Ollie Hampson's sustainable furniture emporium, Priya Misra's handcrafted jewelry boutique, and Eduardo García's farm-to-table food truck.
Ada and James of NextGen Robotics offer affordable automation solutions for small manufacturing units.
Ella Sanderson leads the workshop 'Digital Marketing on a Shoestring Budget'.
A panel discussion titled 'The Future of Home-Grown Economy' is part of the program.
Local banks and microfinance organizations will set up consultation booths to discuss funding opportunities.
Minority-owned businesses and women-led startups are given prominent platforms at the fair.
The 'Youth Entrepreneur Zone' lets teenagers and young adults showcase their business ideas and products.
The 'Green Marketplace' will feature eco-friendly products and sustainable business practices.
Janet Smith sells biodegradable food packaging, and couple Liam and Dana Foster run a 'zero waste' lifestyle store.
The fair is presented as a response to big-box stores and franchises overshadowing home-grown enterprises.
